# fianu_control (Resource)

Manages a Fianu compliance control. Controls define a compliance requirement together with its evaluation logic, policy template, asset scope, and data-source relations. The schema mirrors the on-disk control-package format used by `fianu console deploy`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "fianu_control" "payment_service_sast" {
  path = "payment-service-sast"
  name = "Payment Service SAST"

  detail = {
    full_name   = "Payment Service Static Analysis"
    display_key = "PSSAST"
    description = "Static analysis gates for the payment service repository."
  }
}

# Attaching an attestation form. The questionnaire itself is a fianu_form;
# `detail.form` only references it, and the deploy resolves the reference to
# the form's current active version.
#
# Removing this block does not detach the form — a deploy that omits the
# section means "unchanged" server-side. Detach in the Console.
resource "fianu_control" "vendor_review" {
  path = "vendor-annual-review"
  name = "Vendor Annual Review"

  detail = {
    full_name   = "Vendor Annual Security Review"
    display_key = "VASR"

    form = {
      path = fianu_form.vendor_review.path
    }
  }
}

# Approval rules for exceptions, counted per asset. The first exception on
# each asset for a given CVE approves itself; any repeat on that asset needs
# the control owner. Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins.
resource "fianu_control" "dependabot_alerts" {
  path = "dependabot-alerts"
  name = "Dependabot Alerts"

  detail = {
    full_name   = "No open Dependabot alerts"
    display_key = "DBA"

    # A per-asset history rule must name a measure declared here: an
    # `array.string` list with no `key`, or an `array.object` list whose
    # `keys` include the rule's `key`.
    policy_template = {
      measures = [{
        name = "vulnerabilities"
        type = "section"
        children = [
          { name = "cves", type = "metric", value = "array.string" },
        ]
      }]
    }

    approvals = {
      rules = [{
        id            = "first-exception-per-asset"
        name          = "First exception per asset and CVE auto-approves"
        subject_types = ["exception"]
        # `vulnerabilities.cves` is a list of strings, so no `key`. Drop
        # `measure` to count every exception on the asset instead of per CVE.
        history  = { scope = "asset", measure = "vulnerabilities.cves" }
        criteria = { expressions = ["$history.occurrence == 1"] }
        action   = { type = "auto_approve" }
        }, {
        id            = "repeat-needs-owner"
        name          = "Repeat exceptions need the control owner"
        subject_types = ["exception"]
        action = {
          type         = "require"
          requirements = [{ label = "Control Owner", approvers = ["role:owner@control"], count = 1 }]
        }
      }]
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `detail` (Attributes) Control payload — mirrors the spec.yaml structure used by `fianu console deploy`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail))
- `name` (String) Display name of the entity.
- `path` (String) Human-readable entity key (slug). Immutable — changing this forces replacement.

### Optional

- `children` (List of String) Child entity references. Server-derived; do not author manually.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form key/value metadata. Server may augment with creator/timestamps.
- `parents` (List of String) Parent entity references. Server populates them from cross-entity relationships.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite resource identifier in the form `<entity_type>/<entity_key>` (e.g., `control/payment-service-sast`). Used by `terraform import`.
- `uuid` (String) Server-generated UUID. Stable across versions of the entity.
- `version` (Attributes) Server-managed version envelope. Every partial update bumps `semantic` and regenerates `uuid` + `timestamp` server-side, so the object is NOT pinned via UseStateForUnknown — plans correctly show `(known after apply)` on any change, and Create/Update refetch the entity post-deploy to populate from server truth. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--version))

<a id="nestedatt--detail"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail`

Required:

- `display_key` (String) Short uppercase key (e.g., `CHXST`).
- `full_name` (String) Display name (e.g., `Static Asset Security Analysis`).

Optional:

- `approvals` (Attributes) Approval rules: who must approve requests this entity governs, or when they approve automatically. Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins. Leave unset to keep the rules managed in the Console; set `rules = []` to clear them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals))
- `assets` (Attributes List) Asset types this control evaluates against. Each asset type lists the version `series` (commit, tag, digest, uri, …) the control fires on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--assets))
- `config` (Attributes) Operational configuration — scope of evaluation, retry behavior, evidence/attestation flags. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--config))
- `description` (String) Free-form description of what the control validates.
- `documentation` (Attributes List) External documentation links (vendor docs, runbooks). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--documentation))
- `evaluation` (Attributes List) Evaluation cases — the rego/python/json files that drive control evaluation. Each case mirrors a file in the on-disk control package: `rule.rego`, `rule_test.rego`, `detail.py`, `display.py`, `report.py`, `input/*.json`, `data/*.json`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--evaluation))
- `form` (Attributes) Attestation form for this control — a reference to a `fianu_form`, which supplies the questionnaire an attester fills in. Give exactly one of `path` or `uuid`.

Removing this block does **not** detach the form: a deploy omitting the section means "unchanged" server-side, and the association carries forward to the new control version. Detach in the Console. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--form))
- `policy_template` (Attributes) Policy template — the schema users author policies against. `measures` is the recursive measure tree. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--policy_template))
- `relations` (Attributes List) Subscription relations — which domain/collection this control reads occurrences from, and which plugin produces them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--relations))
- `results` (Attributes) Default result outcomes when the rule emits each verdict. Maps directly to `entities.Results` (a server-side `map[string]bool`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--results))
- `template` (Attributes) Report template for this control — the `template` section of the on-disk package. Both JSON attributes are authored with `jsonencode({...})`; their shapes are owned by the reporting service, so they are passed through rather than modelled here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--template))

<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals`

Required:

- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered rules; the first match wins. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals.rules`

Required:

- `action` (Attributes) What a matching rule does. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--action))
- `id` (String) Stable slug, unique within the block.

Optional:

- `criteria` (Attributes) CEL over `$request`, `$history`, `$series`, `$evidence`, `$subject`, `$target`, `$requester`; unset means always. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--criteria))
- `description` (String) Description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled rule is kept but skipped. Defaults to `true`.
- `enforced` (Boolean) Evaluated before every ordinary rule, farthest governor first, so a domain or collection floor beats a control's auto-approve.
- `history` (Attributes) What counts as the same finding for `$history.occurrence`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--history))
- `name` (String) Display name.
- `subject_types` (List of String) Request kinds the rule applies to; unset means every kind.

<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals.rules.action`

Required:

- `type` (String) `require` or `auto_approve`.

Optional:

- `distinct` (Boolean) Each requirement must be met by a different person.
- `requirements` (Attributes List) One approval condition each (`require` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--action--requirements))

<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--action--requirements"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals.rules.action.requirements`

Required:

- `approvers` (List of String) `user:<sub>`, `role:<relation>`, `role:<relation>@<anchor>` or `role:<relation>@each:<anchor>`; an anchor is `control`, `collection`, `domain`, `subject` or an asset type path.
- `count` (Number) Approvals needed.
- `label` (String) Condition label.



<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--criteria"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals.rules.criteria`

Required:

- `expressions` (List of String) CEL expressions, e.g. `$history.occurrence >= 3`.

Optional:

- `combine_with` (String) `AND` (default) or `OR`.


<a id="nestedatt--detail--approvals--rules--history"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.approvals.rules.history`

Optional:

- `count` (String) `submitted` (default) counts every earlier request; `approved` only approved ones.
- `key` (String) Line-item field identifying a finding, e.g. `alert_id`. Unset when the measure is a list of strings (e.g. CVE ids).
- `max_assets` (Number) With scope `asset`, the most assets a request may cover and still count per asset (default 10, at most 100). A wider request does not match a per-asset auto-approve, so a later rule (e.g. the owner) applies, and it never counts toward its assets' history.
- `measure` (String) List measure holding the line items, e.g. `vulnerabilities.alerts`. Required with scope `control`; with scope `asset`, unset counts every request covering the asset.
- `scope` (String) `control` (default) counts a finding across every asset; `asset` counts per asset the request covers, so the first exception on each asset is occurrence 1. Scope `asset` needs `subject_types` of `exception` and/or `policy`.




<a id="nestedatt--detail--assets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.assets`

Required:

- `type` (String) Asset type — `module`, `repository`, `artifact`, `application`, etc.

Optional:

- `cardinality` (String) Applicability scope. One of `only`, `any`, `a`, `all`. Defaults to `all` server-side.
- `series` (Attributes List) Version series — when this asset type produces evaluable events. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--assets--series))
- `target_asset_type_uuid` (String) Server-side UUID of the asset type. Optional; resolved from `type` when omitted.

<a id="nestedatt--detail--assets--series"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.assets.series`

Required:

- `name` (String) Series name (`commit`, `tag`, `digest`, `uri`).

Optional:

- `code` (Number) Numeric series code. Optional; server assigns from `name` when omitted.



<a id="nestedatt--detail--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.config`

Optional:

- `evidence_submission` (Boolean)
- `manual_attestations` (Boolean)
- `retries` (Boolean)
- `scope` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--detail--documentation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.documentation`

Required:

- `title` (String)
- `url` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--detail--evaluation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.evaluation`

Required:

- `content` (String) Case body — rego/python/JSON content. Use `file("${path.module}/rule.rego")` to load from disk, or an HCL heredoc for inline content.
- `type` (String) Case type. One of `rule`, `rule_test`, `detail`, `display`, `report`, `input`, `data`.

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this case participates in evaluation. Defaults to true when omitted.
- `engine` (String) Evaluation engine for `rule` cases (typically `opa`). Optional; ignored for non-rule cases.
- `label` (String) Optional human-readable label (typically the source filename, e.g., `rule.rego`).


<a id="nestedatt--detail--form"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.form`

Optional:

- `path` (String) Path of the form, e.g. `fianu_form.vendor_review.path`. Resolved to the form's current active version at deploy time.
- `uuid` (String) Entity UUID of the form, e.g. `fianu_form.vendor_review.uuid`. Alternative to `path`.


<a id="nestedatt--detail--policy_template"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.policy_template`

Optional:

- `measures` (Attributes List) Hierarchical policy measure tree. Sections group related metrics; metrics carry a typed `value`. Bounded to 5 levels of nesting. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--policy_template--measures))
- `version` (String) Optional template version label.

<a id="nestedatt--detail--policy_template--measures"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.policy_template.measures`

Required:

- `name` (String) Measure name. Used as the path key when policies reference this measure (e.g., `vulnerabilities.critical.maximum`).
- `type` (String) Either `section` (a grouping with `children`) or `metric` (a leaf carrying a `value`).

Optional:

- `children` (Attributes List) Nested measure children (level 2). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--policy_template--measures--children))
- `description` (String) Optional human-readable description shown in policy authoring UI.
- `keys` (Attributes List) Ordered columns of an `array.object` metric, e.g. `alert_id`. An approval rule's `history.key` must name one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--policy_template--measures--keys))
- `value` (String) Value type for `metric` measures. One of `bool`, `number`, `string`, `array.string`, `array.object`, `regex`. Ignored for `section` measures.

<a id="nestedatt--detail--relations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.relations`

Required:

- `collection` (String) Collection identifier — UUID or path (e.g., `security`, `testing`). Resolved server-side.
- `domain` (String) Domain identifier — UUID or path (e.g., `compliance.controls`). Resolved server-side.

Optional:

- `is_primary` (Boolean) Whether this is the primary relation for the control.
- `note` (String) Note context for this relation (e.g., `occurrence`).
- `path` (String) Subscription I/O path (e.g., `checkmarx.sast`). NOT the collection identifier — this is the producer's path within the collection.
- `producer` (Attributes) The plugin or workflow that produces data for this relation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detail--relations--producer))

<a id="nestedatt--detail--relations--producer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.relations.producer`

Required:

- `path` (String) Producer entity path (e.g., `checkmarx`).
- `type` (String) Producer type — `plugin`, `workflow`, etc.



<a id="nestedatt--detail--results"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.results`

Optional:

- `fail` (Boolean)
- `in_progress` (Boolean)
- `not_required` (Boolean)
- `pass` (Boolean)
- `warn` (Boolean)


<a id="nestedatt--detail--template"></a>
### Nested Schema for `detail.template`

Required:

- `template_content` (String) TemplateSpec object as JSON. Two modes: `{ mode = "wizard", ... }` for structured block instructions the backend compiles to a Go template, or `{ mode = "raw", ... }` for passthrough Go `html/template` source. Author with `jsonencode({...})`, or `jsondecode(file("..."))` re-encoded if the spec lives on disk.

Optional:

- `schema_snapshot` (String) Cached JSON Schema produced by running `report.py` against test fixtures, so the template editor does not re-execute it on every load. Optional — the server regenerates it when absent.
- `template_name` (String) Optional human-readable label for the template.



<a id="nestedatt--version"></a>
### Nested Schema for `version`

Read-Only:

- `semantic` (String) Semantic version (e.g., `1.0.0` or `5`).
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state. May be mutated by server-side workflows.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status. May be mutated by server-side workflows.
- `timestamp` (String) RFC3339 timestamp the version was created.
- `uuid` (String) Per-version UUID. Changes whenever the server creates a new version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Import an existing Fianu control into Terraform state.
# The composite ID is `<entity_type>/<entity_key>` — the same form `terraform
# state list` will display.

terraform import fianu_control.payment_service_sast control/payment-service-sast
```
